paper.title: Your Code Agent Can Grow Alongside You with Structured Memory
paper.central_claim: MemCoder: structuring a repository's historical human commits into agent-friendly memory, retrieving it with a dual-stage retriever, refining execution with a test-writing Refining Sub-agent, and internalizing human-validated solutions into long-term memory enables continual human-AI co-evolution and reaches SOTA on SWE-bench Verified (DeepSeek-V3.2 68.4% to 77.8%).

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; model type per claude-kimi config (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

evidence.quote: Crucially, an experience self-internalization mechanism is introduced to crystallize human-validated solutions into long-term knowledge, thereby supporting sustained evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Central retention claim: human-validated solutions are written into long-term memory.

evidence.quote: existing systems fail to internalize human-verified solutions.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap; the changed non-weight object is the memory store of verified solutions.

evidence.quote: In contrast to these rigid or decay-based structures, MemCoder introduces a flat, autonomous memory management paradigm that dynamically integrates new insights.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory is flat and append-oriented, versus MemoryBank/SAGE with forgetting and RAPTOR-type hierarchies; delta against memory-for-agents work is stated only at this level.

evidence.quote: To ensure a fair evaluation and prevent temporal leakage, we strictly restrict the agent at test time to retrieve only historical experiences created prior to the corresponding test issue.
evidence.support_explanation: Temporal hold-out for memory; enforcement mechanism and audit are not described.

evidence.quote: generate higher-quality, repository-aligned code without modifying long-term memory during execution.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-refinement is in-episode only; no persistent change from refinement.

evidence.quote: Unlike historical commits, these experiences originate from model-generated solutions and human validation, enabling the memory to gradually shift from human-only priors to human–agent co-evolved knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Internalization is a set union M_{N+1} = M_N + m_{N+1} with no stated gate beyond human validation, no merge, retirement or conflict handling.

evidence.quote: demonstrates that all three proposed modules contribute positively to the performance enhancement of MemCoder
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2: full 77.8 (389); w/o DSR 76.4 (382); w/o DSR and ER 73.0 (365); w/o CR 71.6 (358); w/o all 68.4 (342). Differences from DSR are 7 instances.

evidence.quote: Ablation study of MemCoder on the SWE-bench Verified dataset using DeepSeek-V3.2.
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation is on one backbone and one run; cumulative removals, no w/o ER alone.

evidence.quote: (i) No historical experience; (ii) Raw commits and patch records without structuring; and (iii) Structured memory polished by an LLM.
evidence.support_explanation: Controlled representation comparison under otherwise fixed variables: none 68.4, raw 73.0 (w/o DSR and ER), structured 76.4 (w/o DSR).

evidence.quote: While the official OpenHands results are reported under pass@
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 compares MemCoder at pass@1/pass@2 against OpenHands numbers taken from official reports at pass@3 with different backbones; no re-run under matched scaffold version or attempts.

evidence.quote: We conduct experiments under the pass@1 evaluation protocol.
evidence.support_explanation: Single attempt per instance; no seeds or repeated runs stated.

evidence.quote: evaluated on a randomly sampled 200-instance subset of the SWE-bench Verified dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval sweeps use a 200-instance subset, single run.

evidence.quote: including memory construction, experience retrieval, iterative refinement, and experience internalization with human assistance.
evidence.support_explanation: The loop includes human assistance; internalization is part of the pipeline description only.

evidence.quote: undergoes human review before the commit is finalized
evidence.support_explanation: Internalization gate is a human review; the new commit is learned only at the next Stage-1 sync, and no experiment exercises this.

evidence.quote: We follow the official evaluation methodology provided by SWE-bench.
evidence.support_explanation: Resolution judged by executing unit tests via the official sb-cli; credible verifier.

evidence.quote: significantly dilutes the signal-to-noise ratio of valid evidence, introducing unnecessary context overhead.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors report that too large top-k hurts; retrieval noise and cost trade-off acknowledged but no token or dollar cost.

evidence.quote: raw commits are distilled into reference solutions.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory is built by an LLM from human commit history, not from the agent's own execution outcomes.

evidence.quote: is autonomously synthesized by the agent based on its internal reasoning state and task context.
evidence.support_explanation: The agent decides when and what to retrieve via a repo_commit_search tool with progressive top-k.

evidence.quote: delivers a 9.4% improvement in resolved rate over the general foundation model DeepSeek-V3.2
evidence.support_explanation: Matches Table 2 (68.4 to 77.8, i.e. 9.4 points); attributable to retrieval, structuring and refinement, not to the internalization mechanism.

signatures.object: Long-term memory M of structured commit entries (keywords, problem, root cause, solution); baseline: no memory or raw commits
signatures.information: Repository commit messages and diffs (human-authored), test-time issue text; temporal cutoff before each issue
signatures.operation: LLM structures each commit into a sextuple; ANN search plus cross-encoder rerank; agent chooses when to call retrieval and with which query
signatures.output: Retrieved entries injected into the primary agent context
signatures.conditions: top-k chosen by agent with progressive schedule (prompt: initial 8, then n*8)
signatures.feedback: None for construction (human history); verification feedback only in-episode
signatures.selection_rule_data: Reranker score only; no utility-based admission
signatures.persistence: Vector DB; new commits synchronised at Stage 1
signatures.claimed_effect: w/o CR 71.6 vs 77.8; raw vs structured memory 73.0 vs 76.4
signatures.failure_boundary: top-k too large dilutes context; plateau reported

signatures.object: Refining Sub-agent output (test code and verification checklist), in-episode only
signatures.information: Problem, trajectory, environment feedback, retrieved precedents
signatures.operation: LLM writes reproduction tests and a checklist, executes them, returns result to primary agent
signatures.output: Checklist and test result in context
signatures.persistence: None; memory not modified during execution

signatures.object: Memory update by self-internalization of human-reviewed agent solutions
signatures.operation: Commit then re-ingest at next sync (set union)
signatures.failure_boundary: No dedup, conflict, retirement, or error-propagation analysis

gap.author_gap: Code agents operate on static snapshots, ignore human defect-repair history in version control and discard human-verified solutions.
gap.checked_gap: Using commit history as retrieved precedent is a real but well-trodden fixed object; the specific remaining bottleneck (agent-friendly structuring and verifiable refinement) is partly supported by Table 2, while the internalization gap is not tested.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Cited: MemoryBank, SAGE, RAPTOR, MemWalker, A-mem, MemInsight, APE, OPRO, ReAct, Self-Refine (paper Sec 2, v1). Not discussed (our_inference, not verified here): other experience-memory methods built specifically for SWE-bench agents and repository-history retrieval work.
gap.residue: How a code agent's own verified fixes should be admitted, merged and retired.
gap.stakes: Repeated errors and loss of tacit repository conventions; shown only through resolved-rate gain from retrieval.
gap.method_response: Structured commit memory, agent-driven retrieval, test-writing refinement, human-reviewed write-back.
gap.remaining_gap: Write-back loop untested; no gate, conflict or retirement; memory source is human commits rather than agent feedback.
unresolved: effect of internalization over a task stream

G.reason: Real but well-trodden gap (static code agents ignoring repository history); neighbours cited are mostly generic memory work, and the internalization gap is not backed by a measured failure.

M.reason: Structure-then-retrieve-then-verify chain is concrete and partly tested, but write-back is a bare set union with no mechanism for admission or error control.

X.reason: Retrieval pipeline and prompts reconstructable; write-back gate, merge, conflict, retirement and versioning are absent, and the human-review step is unspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Resolved status is determined by executing official SWE-bench tests via sb-cli with instance counts reported; leaderboard comparison mixing pass@k is a separate causality issue.

E.causality.reason: Cumulative ablations and a none/raw/structured comparison isolate retrieval and structuring, but the evolution claim has no test, baselines are copied pass@3 numbers, and no alternative retrieval or memory method is compared.

E.holdout.reason: Temporal restriction of retrievable history is a sensible hold-out but is asserted without enforcement details, and backbone contamination of SWE-bench Verified is unexamined.

E.statistics.reason: Instance counts are given but there is a single pass@1 run and no intervals; ablation steps of 7 instances are untested for noise.

E.cost.reason: Retrieval frequency and retrieved-entry counts shown for a 200-instance sweep, but no token or dollar cost, memory construction cost over full histories, or matched attempts for baselines.
